who: GPT-6 Astra Pro, distributed compile review
what: Source acceptance run 46056228918 reported corrupted double-linked list and a native SIGSEGV in the launcher control thread while running transient_accept_errors_leave_the_reactor_available_to_healthy_clients. The retained report has an unmapped native PC and an unreadable caller frame, but no raw fault registers, same-process native maps, native-library identities or core. Up::Fault already carried the registers transiently; the test driver retained only the formatted report.
cost: Later passing processes cannot resolve the failed process's ASLR-dependent PC. The original corruption remains unexplained despite the later diagnostic passing that control, and the performance candidate's failed acceptance cannot be cleared by the separate stale-miss fix.
cause: The retained fault presentation loses the raw machine-state evidence when no placed guest function or readable caller identifies the fault.
whys: The native fault could not be attributed to an instruction or caller.
The original artifact had no native mapping or readable caller and omitted the captured register values.
The driver decoded Up::Fault but persisted only run_fault::Report text.
The report prioritizes placed guest functions and caller walking, which supplied neither identity for this fault.
Diagnostic retention was not held to preserving the evidence needed for a failure outside placed guest code.
class: lossy fault presentation discards machine-state evidence needed for native crash attribution
prevention: Retain the existing bounded raw fault message, same-process native mappings and library identities on the next natural full pooled source-protocol run; a bounded core would additionally retain heap metadata. Preserve scheduling and compiler mode so the capture does not become a serialization experiment.
fix: No speculative allocator or ownership change. The bounded source audit found no supported corrupting path; the paired stale-miss regression proves only the separate duplicate-tail repair.
state: Open. The original heap-corruption and helper-entry failures remain unproved; later passes and the admission fix are not recorded as their resolution.
